title: API · Assets
description: List all tokenized assets, or fetch one by id.
content: Assets

title: API · Assets › List assets
content: Returns an array of asset objects. Query parameters (all optional) Name Type Notes asset_type string Filter by class: real_estate , invoice , commodity active boolean Filter by active status curl "http://localhost:8080/assets?asset_type=real_estate&active=true" Response schema (per asset): Field Type Notes id number Registry id token_contract string Asset-token contract issuer string Issuer account name string symbol string asset_type string real_estate \ invoice \ commodity description string valuation_cents string USD cents ( i128 ) valuation_usd number Dollars, convenience decimals number total_supply string Base units ( i128 ) holders number Addresses with a positive balance active boolean paused boolean compliance_contract string Gate for this asset created_at_ledger number Example curl http://localhost:8080/assets [ { "id": 1, "token_contract": "CBMCWLSQSWUTLUJFCNBHNBSXMUM3XU7NAQ5TSNERW4HA4ZZBYHLG4ECZ", "issuer": "GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA", "name": "Manhattan Loft", "symbol": "MLOFT", "asset_type": "real_estate", "description": "A tokenized loft in Manhattan", "valuation_cents": "500000000", "valuation_usd": 5000000.0, "decimals": 2, "total_supply": "1000000", "holders": 1, "active": true, "paused": false, "compliance_contract": "CBUERYDM7DXTZLLKDBRJKUBPFJ7M4OSUN4T7XKUARU345RLXNAIQD2IU", "created_at_ledger": 3502885 } ]

title: API · Assets › Get an asset
content: Path parameters Name Type Notes id number Registry id (e.g. 1 ) Example curl http://localhost:8080/assets/1 Returns a single asset object with the schema above. Errors { "error": "not_found", "message": "no asset with id 999" } Returned with status 404 when no asset has the given id. A non-numeric id ( /assets/abc ) is rejected with 400 by the router. total_supply and valuation_cents are strings. In JavaScript, parse them with BigInt(asset.total_supply) and compute a display value as Number(BigInt(asset.total_supply)) / 10 ** asset.decimals .

title: API · Filtering and sorting assets
description: Filter and sort the asset list server-side.
content: Filtering and sorting assets GET /v1/assets accepts these query parameters: Parameter Values Description asset_type e.g. real_estate Only assets of this class. active true , false Only active or inactive assets. sort valuation Sort by USD valuation (ordered by valuation_cents in USD cents). order asc , desc (default) Direction; requires sort . fields comma-separated field names Return only these fields (partial response). offset , limit integers Pagination (limit defaults to 50, max 100). curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets?asset_type=real_estate&sort=valuation&order=asc" Invalid or unknown parameters return 400 with the shared error body: { "error": { "code": "bad_request", "message": "unknown query parameter: foo" } } See API · Error Bodies for the canonical error shape and the full list of error codes.

title: API · Filtering and sorting assets › Empty results
content: When no assets match the supplied filters, GET /v1/assets returns 200 with an empty JSON array — never null and never an error: [] curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets?asset_type=real_estate&active=false" 200 OK [] Malformed or out-of-range parameters (for example a non-integer limit , an unknown sort value, or order without sort ) still return 400 with the shared error body {"error": "invalid_parameter", "message": "..."} — an empty result set is only returned for valid parameters that match nothing.

title: API · Filtering and sorting assets › Field selection
content: Combine ?fields= with the filter and sort parameters to trim each item in the response to just the fields you need. Filtering and sorting still apply to the full record set before the projection is applied. curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets?asset_type=real_estate&sort=valuation&order=asc&fields=id,symbol,valuation_usd" An unknown field name returns 400 with a body of the form: {"error": "invalid_parameter", "message": "unknown field ..."} See API · Field Selection for the full list of selectable fields and projection rules.

title: API · Compliance
description: Non-PII compliance summary for a tokenized asset.
content: Compliance Returns an aggregate view of an asset's KYC allowlist. It deliberately exposes counts, not addresses — no personally identifying information leaves the API. Path parameters Name Type Notes id number Registry id Response schema Field Type Notes total_records number Addresses ever added to the allowlist approved number Currently passing is_allowed suspended number rejected number pending number with_expiry number Records with a non-zero expires_at jurisdictions array { jurisdiction, count } breakdown Example curl http://localhost:8080/assets/1/compliance { "total_records": 1, "approved": 1, "suspended": 0, "rejected": 0, "pending": 0, "with_expiry": 0, "jurisdictions": [ { "jurisdiction": "US", "count": 1 } ] } Errors Returns 404 with { "error": "not_found", … } when the asset id is unknown. An asset's holder set can itself be sensitive. This endpoint gives issuers and analysts the shape of an allowlist — how many are approved, where they're based, how many approvals carry expiries — without publishing who they are. The per-address KYC records live only on-chain and in the issuer's own tooling. The jurisdictions breakdown reflects the jurisdiction field of each KYC record. Combined with the contract's is_jurisdiction_blocked , it helps issuers audit their geographic exposure. See the Compliance Guide . Backing contract This summary is derived from the compliance contract's KYC allowlist. The approved count corresponds to records passing the contract's is_allowed check, and the jurisdictions breakdown reads each record's jurisdiction field alongside is_jurisdiction_blocked . See the Compliance contract reference for the full set of functions and their semantics.

title: API · Dividends
description: Distribution history for a tokenized asset.
content: Dividends Returns every dividend distribution created for the asset's token, ordered by creation ledger (newest first). Path parameters Name Type Notes id number Registry id Response schema (per distribution): Field Type Notes id number Distribution id asset_token string The asset paid out on payment_token string Token used to pay total_amount string Pool size, base units ( i128 ) distributed string Claimed so far, base units ( i128 ) claimed_percent number 0–100 (2 dp) completed boolean true once fully claimed snapshot_ledger number Ledger at creation created_at_ledger number Example curl http://localhost:8080/assets/1/dividends [ { "id": 1, "asset_token": "CBMCWLSQSWUTLUJFCNBHNBSXMUM3XU7NAQ5TSNERW4HA4ZZBYHLG4ECZ", "payment_token": "CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC", "total_amount": "100000000000", "distributed": "25000000000", "claimed_percent": 25.0, "completed": false, "snapshot_ledger": 3510000, "created_at_ledger": 3510000 } ] An asset with no distributions returns an empty array [] . Errors Returns 404 with { "error": "not_found", … } when the asset id is unknown. total_amount and distributed are in the payment token's base units, not the asset token's. Classic Stellar assets (SACs) use 7 decimals, so 100000000000 above is 10,000.0 units of the payment token.

title: API · Error Bodies
description: The single JSON error shape returned by every route of the Stellar RWA API, with the full list of error codes.
content: Error Bodies This page is the single canonical reference for the error response shape of the Stellar RWA API. Every other page links here instead of restating the shape.

title: API · Error Bodies › The shape
content: Every error response, from any route or from the server itself, has the same JSON shape and an application/json content type: { "error": "not_found", "message": "no asset with id 999" } Field Type Unit Nullable Description error string — No Stable, machine-readable code. Branch on this. message string — No Human-readable explanation. Do not parse it. The body contains exactly these two fields. Headers such as Retry-After are preserved on the response. The shape is enforced centrally ( api/src/routes/error_body.rs ): every error path is normalized to it, including - router-level 404 (unknown route) and 405 (method not allowed) responses, - query-string and path-parameter rejections ( 400 ), - request timeouts ( 408 ) and request-body size limits ( 413 ), - the per-IP rate limiter ( 429 ), - /metrics bearer-token auth failures ( 401 ), - unexpected server errors ( 500 ) and unavailability ( 503 ).

title: API · Error Bodies › Error codes
content: HTTP status error When 400 bad_request Malformed query string or path parameter 400 invalid_parameter A ?fields= value names an unknown field; message lists the available fields 401 unauthorized /metrics called without a valid bearer token 404 not_found Unknown asset, distribution or route 405 method_not_allowed Any method other than GET 408 request_timeout The request exceeded the server timeout 413 payload_too_large The request body exceeded the size limit 429 too_many_requests The per-IP rate limit was exceeded 500 internal_server_error Unexpected server error 503 service_unavailable The service cannot answer right now GET /health is a status report rather than an error: it returns its own JSON status document, with a 503 status while the snapshot is stale.

title: API · Error Bodies › Invalid field selection
content: When a ?fields= value names a field the endpoint does not expose, the response is a 400 with the invalid_parameter code. The message lists the fields that are available, so a client can correct the request: { "error": "invalid_parameter", "message": "unknown field \"symbl\"; available fields: id, symbol, name, issuer, status" } See Field Selection for the full syntax and per-endpoint examples.

title: API · Error Bodies › Request IDs
content: request_id is not part of the error body. The request identifier is returned in the X-Request-Id response header only, so the body stays exactly two fields. See Request IDs for how to read and use it.

title: API · Events
description: Recent contract events emitted by the indexer.
content: Events The API exposes a compact event stream for clients that need to react to state changes without polling the full asset list. The payload is a JSON array ordered newest-first. curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/events?limit=20" [ { "id": 42, "contract": "CDL...", "event_type": "Transfer", "ledger": 3514152, "timestamp": "2026-07-09T08:43:12.101772791+00:00", "data": { "from": "GA...", "to": "GB...", "amount": "100" } } ] Field selection: Use the fields query parameter to return only the event fields you need. See Field Selection for the full syntax. curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/events?limit=20&fields=id,event_type,ledger" [ { "id": 42, "event_type": "Transfer", "ledger": 3514152 } ] Requesting a field that does not exist on Event returns a 400 error with code invalid_parameter : { "error": "invalid_parameter", "message": "Unknown field: 'foo'" } Response schema ( Event , per event): Field Type Unit Nullable Description id integer Event id No Indexer-assigned event id contract string — No Contract address that emitted the event event_type string — No Event name ledger integer Ledger sequence No Ledger containing the event timestamp string RFC 3339 timestamp Yes JSON null when the ledger timestamp is unavailable data JSON value — No Raw event payload Each event includes the contract address, event name, ledger, timestamp (when available), and the raw payload emitted by the contract.

title: API · Events › Ordering and pagination
content: Ordering. The response is sorted newest-first: descending by ledger , then descending by id within the same ledger. The order is applied by this API's indexer, not passed through from Soroban RPC. The indexer polls Soroban RPC getEvents every 10 seconds. RPC returns events oldest-first, and the indexer merges each new batch into its buffer and re-sorts the whole buffer on every poll. No cursor. limit is the only paging parameter. It defaults to 50 , and values above 200 are capped at 200 rather than rejected. The endpoint has no cursor or offset parameter and sends no Link header. If you pass cursor , it is silently ignored. Every request returns the newest limit events from an in-memory buffer that holds at most 200 events. You cannot page further back than that buffer. Stability across polls. Results are not a stable page. Each successful indexer poll (at most every 10 seconds) adds new events to the front of the list, and once the buffer is full the oldest events drop off the end. The same request can therefore return different events from one poll to the next. Keep these limits in mind: - Responses are fixed between polls. Two responses with the same ETag ( "ledger- " , the last indexed ledger) have identical bodies. A failed RPC cycle keeps the previous list unchanged, so the buffer never shrinks or empties because of an RPC error. - id is not a unique key. The indexer takes id from the leading segment of the RPC event id, so several events (for example the items of one batch_* call) can share the same id and ledger . To track your position, use ledger as a high-water mark, not id . - Events can be missed. If more events land between two of your polls than the buffer holds, the overflow is gone and cannot be fetched again. The buffer is also in memory only, so it starts empty after a restart. If you need complete history, read Soroban RPC getEvents directly, which serves events only within the RPC node's retention window. Polling example. Each indexer poll ingests whole ledgers, so a ledger high-water mark is enough to pick out only the events you have not seen yet: Poll 1: take the newest events and note the highest ledger seen curl -i "$API_BASE_URL/v1/events?limit=200" HTTP/1.1 200 OK ETag: "ledger-3514160" [ { "id": 42, "ledger": 3514152, ... }, { "id": 41, "ledger": 3514150, ... } ] -> store LAST_LEDGER=3514152 and ETAG='"ledger-3514160"' Poll 2 (10 seconds or more later): send the ETag back curl -i -H 'If-None-Match: "ledger-3514160"' "$API_BASE_URL/v1/events?limit=200" HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified -> nothing new; keep your state or HTTP/1.1 200 OK with a new ETag -> keep only events with ledger > LAST_LEDGER let lastLedger = 0; let etag: string null = null; async function poll() { const res = await fetch( ${API_BASE_URL}/v1/events?limit=200 , { headers: etag ? { "If-None-Match": etag } : {}, }); if (res.status === 304) return []; etag = res.headers.get("ETag"); const events: Array = await res.json(); const fresh = events.filter((e) => e.ledger > lastLedger); // If every returned event is new and the page is full, older new events were lost. if (lastLedger > 0 && events.length === 200 && fresh.length === events.length) { console.warn("Event buffer rolled past your last poll; some events were missed."); } if (events.length > 0) lastLedger = Math.max(lastLedger, events[0].ledger); return fresh.reverse(); // oldest-first for processing } Order: newest-first by ledger , then id . Page size: limit , default 50, capped at 200. Cursor: none, and cursor and Link are not supported. Stability: bodies are identical for the same ETag , the list changes after each successful 10-second indexer poll, and the 200-event window rolls forward, so poll often enough and use ledger as your high-water mark.

title: API · Events › Worked example
content: The following script fetches the latest events from the current Testnet deployment and prints a compact summary. To poll for new events, see Ordering and pagination . The amount table below shows how to convert Transfer amounts using the token's decimals. Set the base URL for the current Testnet deployment Fetch the first page of events curl -s "$API_BASE_URL/v1/events?limit=5" jq . const API_BASE_URL = process.env.API_BASE_URL ?? "https://api.testnet.example.com"; async function fetchEvents(limit = 20) { const res = await fetch( ${API_BASE_URL}/v1/events?limit=${limit} ); if (!res.ok) { throw new Error( Events request failed: ${res.status} ${res.statusText} ); } return res.json(); } const events = await fetchEvents(5); for (const event of events) { console.log( #${event.id} ${event.event_type} @ ledger ${event.ledger} ); } Run the snippet above with API_BASE_URL pointed at the current Testnet deployment. A successful response returns a JSON array of events (possibly empty on a fresh deployment or right after a restart), newest first. Event payload amount units: Amounts inside data depend on the contract and event type, in accordance with the contracts specification : Event type Amount field Unit / Base Conversion Transfer , Mint , Burn data.amount Asset token base units ( i128 string) Number(BigInt(data.amount)) / 10 token.decimals Valuation data.new_valuation USD cents ( i128 string) Number(BigInt(data.new_valuation)) / 100 Dividend created data.total_amount Payment token base units ( i128 string) Number(BigInt(data.total_amount)) / 10 payment_token.decimals Dividend claim data.amount Payment token base units ( i128 string) Number(BigInt(data.amount)) / 10 payment_token.decimals // For a Transfer event with amount = "100" and token decimals = 2: const rawAmount = BigInt(event.data.amount); const displayAmount = Number(rawAmount) / (10 2); // => 1.00 token

title: API · Events › Errors
content: Every error response uses the shared two-field body shape: { "error": "invalid_limit", "message": "limit must be between 1 and 100" } Field Type Description error string Stable, machine-readable error code message string Human-readable description of the problem See Errors for the canonical error shape, the full list of codes, and the HTTP status codes each one maps to. Event types by entry point: The indexer records one event per state-changing contract entry point. The table below maps the current contract surface to the event_type values you will see on this endpoint. See the Asset Token Contract and Dividends references for the full entry-point definitions. Entry point event_type Notes transfer , transfer_from Transfer SEP-41 token transfer; data.amount in asset base units mint Mint SEP-41 issuance; data.amount in asset base units burn , burn_from Burn SEP-41 redemption; data.amount in asset base units approve , allowance Approve SEP-41 allowance update; data.amount in asset base units batch_transfer , batch_mint , batch_burn Transfer , Mint , Burn One event per item in the batch, sharing the same ledger set_valuation Valuation data.new_valuation in USD cents set_min_holding_period MinHoldingPeriodUpdated data.min_holding_period in seconds transfer_admin , accept_admin , renounce_admin AdminTransferInitiated , AdminTransferred , AdminRenounced Two-step admin handover create_dividend created data.total_amount in payment token base units claim_dividend claim data.amount in payment token base units set_dividend_deadline DividendDeadlineUpdated data.deadline is a ledger sequence reclaim_dividend DividendReclaimed data.amount in payment token base units cancel_dividend DividendCancelled data.dividend_id identifies the cancelled dividend Batch entry points emit one event per item rather than a single aggregate event. Filter by event_type and group by ledger to reconstruct a batch.

title: API · Events › Glossary
content: New to Stellar or this API? These terms appear throughout the page: - Ledger sequence — a monotonically increasing integer identifying a ledger (a batch of transactions) on the Stellar network. Higher numbers are more recent. See Time & Ledgers . - RFC 3339 timestamp — the standard date/time string format used for timestamp , e.g. 2026-07-09T08:43:12.101772791+00:00 . - i128 — a 128-bit signed integer. Soroban contracts encode large amounts as i128 ; the API serializes them as decimal strings so no precision is lost in JSON. - Base units — the smallest indivisible unit of a token. Divide by 10 ** decimals to get the human-readable amount (e.g. a token with 2 decimals stores 100 base units as 1.00 ). - SEP-41 — the Stellar token interface standard that defines transfer , mint , burn , and approve entry points. - Entry point — a callable contract function. Each state-changing entry point emits one event. - High-water mark — the highest ledger a client has already processed. This endpoint has no cursor, so clients poll and keep only events whose ledger is above their mark. See Ordering and pagination .

title: API · Field selection
description: Request partial responses with the fields parameter.
content: Field selection Every JSON data endpoint under /v1 (assets, holders, events, dividends and single-record endpoints) accepts ?fields= with a comma-separated list of field names. Each returned object then contains only those fields. curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets?fields=id,symbol,valuation_usd" curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets/1/holders?fields=address,balance" Fields are validated against the first record of a list, so an empty list is returned as-is.

title: API · Field selection › Examples per list endpoint
content: Endpoint Example GET /v1/assets curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets?fields=id,symbol,valuation_usd" GET /v1/assets?query=... (filtered assets) curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets?query=USDC&fields=id,symbol,issuer" GET /v1/assets/{id}/holders curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets/1/holders?fields=address,balance,decimals" GET /v1/assets/{id}/dividends curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets/1/dividends?fields=id,amount,asset_code" GET /v1/events curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/events?fields=id,type,ledger,created_at" GET /v1/compliance curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/compliance?fields=asset_id,status,updated_at"

title: API · Field selection › Invalid field names
content: Requesting a field that does not exist returns HTTP 400 with an invalid_parameter error. The message lists the fields that are available for that endpoint: curl -i "$API_BASE_URL/v1/assets?fields=nope" { "error": "invalid_parameter", "message": "unknown field nope ; available fields: ..." } See API · Errors for the full error envelope and other status codes.

title: API · Field selection › Empty results
content: When a query matches nothing, the endpoint still returns 200 with a well-formed empty body: an empty array ( [] ) for list endpoints, or an empty object ( {} ) for single-record endpoints. It never returns null and never turns an empty result into an error. Because fields is validated against the first record of a list, validation is skipped when the list is empty — an empty list is returned as-is regardless of the requested field names. When selecting amount fields like balance , remember that values are returned in raw base units. If you plan to format the balance for display, include decimals in your field list (or query the parent asset) so you can convert balance / 10 ** decimals . Similarly, note that valuation_cents is in USD cents while valuation_usd is in USD dollars.

title: API · Health & Indexer Lag
description: How GET /health reports the last successful poll, ledger lag and staleness.
content: Health & indexer lag GET /health returns 200 with "status": "ok" while the indexer is polling normally, and 503 with "status": "degraded" when it has stalled. Field Type Unit Nullable Meaning status string — No ok or degraded snapshot_age_seconds integer Seconds Yes Age of the served snapshot; JSON null before a successful refresh max_age_seconds integer Seconds No Stall threshold consecutive_failures integer Failed polls No Consecutive failed polls since the last success last_poll_at string RFC 3339 timestamp Yes Time of the last successful poll; JSON null before one succeeds last_poll_age_seconds integer Seconds Yes Seconds since the last successful poll; JSON null before one succeeds last_indexed_ledger integer Ledger sequence No Ledger reached by the last successful poll; 0 before one succeeds ledger_lag integer Ledgers Yes Estimated ledgers closed since that poll; JSON null before one succeeds

title: API · Health & Indexer Lag › Threshold
content: The indexer is reported unhealthy when the last successful poll is older than max_age_seconds . The default is three poll intervals (30 seconds). Override it with the RWA_HEALTH_MAX_POLL_AGE_SECS environment variable.

title: API · Health & Indexer Lag › Staleness during an RPC outage
content: The indexer counts consecutive failed polls and reports the count as consecutive_failures in /health . While polls are failing, or the last successful poll is older than the threshold, every response carries: - X-Data-Stale: true - X-Data-Age-Seconds : seconds since the last successful poll - X-Indexer-Consecutive-Failures : current failure streak The previous snapshot keeps being served. When a poll succeeds again, the headers disappear and the recovery is logged.

title: API · Health & Indexer Lag › Error responses
content: GET /health returns its own status document even on 503 : the body is the same field set shown above with "status": "degraded" , not the shared error body. Any other error from this route (for example a 500 from an internal failure) uses the shared error shape documented in Errors .

title: API · Holder position
content: Holder position Returns a holder's positions and claimable dividends across every asset in a single request. Use it to render a portfolio view without issuing one request per asset.

title: API · Holder position › Request
content: GET /v1/holders/:address/position Path parameters: Parameter Type Required Description address string Yes Stellar account address of the holder There are no query parameters. The response always covers every asset in which the address holds a positive balance. curl "$API_BASE_URL/v1/holders/$ADDRESS/position"

title: API · Holder position › Example response
content: { "address": "G...", "asset_count": 1, "total_value_usd": 50.0, "positions": [ { "asset_id": 1, "asset_name": "Test Asset", "symbol": "TST", "balance": "250", "share_percent": 25.0, "value_usd": 50.0, "claimable": [ { "distribution_id": 7, "payment_token": "C...", "amount": "200" } ] } ] }

title: API · Holder position › Response
content: Response schema ( HolderPosition ): Field Type Unit Nullable Description address string — No Holder account address asset_count integer Assets No Number of returned positions total_value_usd number USD No Sum of position values positions PositionEntry[] One entry per asset No Positions are sorted by balance, largest first PositionEntry fields: Field Type Unit Nullable Description asset_id integer Registry id No asset_name string — No symbol string — No Asset-token symbol balance string Asset-token base units No Exact balance as a decimal string share_percent number Percent No Share of total supply value_usd number USD No Estimated value of the position claimable Claimable[] One entry per open distribution No Estimated claim amounts Claimable fields: Field Type Unit Nullable Description distribution_id integer Distribution id No payment_token string — No Payment-token contract address amount string Payment-token base units No Estimated unclaimed amount as a decimal string - value_usd is the holder's share_percent of the asset valuation. - claimable lists each open distribution with the holder's pro-rata share ( balance / total_supply ) of the unclaimed pool, in payment-token base units. It is an estimate from indexed data, not an on-chain claim quote. - An address with no holdings returns HTTP 200 with a well-formed body: asset_count is 0 , total_value_usd is 0 , and positions is [] — an empty array, never null and never an error. Clients can rely on this shape and iterate positions without a null check.

title: API · Holder position › Errors
content: Error responses use the shared two-field error body ( error and message ) defined in error_body.rs . See API · Errors for the canonical shape and the full list of codes. Status error When 400 bad_request The :address path segment is not a valid Stellar account address 429 too_many_requests The rate limit for this endpoint was exceeded { "error": "bad_request", "message": "invalid Stellar account address" }

title: API · Holder position › Empty positions
content: An address with no holdings returns asset_count: 0 , total_value_usd: 0 , and an empty positions array: { "address": "G...", "asset_count": 0, "total_value_usd": 0.0, "positions": [] } claimable amounts are computed from indexed data at the time of the request. They are not an on-chain claim quote: balances, distribution state, or the unclaimed pool may change between this response and a subsequent claim call. For an exact amount, call the dividend contract's claimable function live — see the Integration Guide . Because asset tokens and payment tokens may use different decimal bases, always scale each amount using its corresponding token decimals: // 1. Convert asset token balance (e.g. TST with decimals = 2): const rawBalance = BigInt(position.balance); // "250" const assetDecimals = 2; const displayBalance = Number(rawBalance) / (10 assetDecimals); // => 2.50 TST // 2. Convert claimable dividend (e.g. USDC payment token with decimals = 7): const rawClaimable = BigInt(position.claimable[0].amount); // "200" const paymentDecimals = 7; const displayClaimable = Number(rawClaimable) / (10 paymentDecimals); // => 0.0000200 USDC

title: API · Holders
description: Holder list with balances for a tokenized asset.
content: Holders Returns every address that is on the asset's compliance allowlist and holds a positive balance. The asset-token contract does not enumerate holders directly, so the indexer derives this from the allowlist intersected with balances. Path parameters Name Type Notes id number Registry id Response schema (per holder): Field Type Notes address string Holder account balance string Base units ( i128 ) share_percent number Percent of total supply, 0–100 (2 dp) Example curl http://localhost:8080/assets/1/holders [ { "address": "GAIQGTOBTTLLDJ4SWGGESM7UWJ2DI4K3ZNHUSHPDKJL2IE5FKY3BSRAA", "balance": "1000000", "share_percent": 100.0 } ] Errors Returns 404 with { "error": "not_found", … } when the asset id is unknown. An asset with holders but none currently holding a positive balance returns an empty array [] . Holders are sorted by balance, largest first. share_percent is computed from balance / total_supply at index time, so it reflects the most recent 10-second refresh.

title: API Overview
description: How the read-only Stellar RWA indexing API works, and its conventions.
content: API Overview The Stellar RWA API is a read-only REST service that indexes all tokenized asset activity on Stellar and serves it as JSON. It is written in Rust (Axum + tokio) and holds no keys — it never signs or submits transactions. Base URL (local): http://localhost:8080

title: API Overview › How indexing works
content: A background task polls Soroban RPC every 10 seconds. On each tick it reads the current state of the four contracts by simulating view calls — get_all_assets on the registry, then per-asset get_metadata , get_allowlist , balance and get_distributions_for_asset — and rebuilds an in-memory snapshot. State is kept in memory (no database in v1). If the RPC is briefly unreachable, the indexer logs the error, keeps serving the last good snapshot, and retries on the next tick. The API never panics on a transient failure.

title: API Overview › Conventions
content: - Large integers are strings. Token amounts and valuations are i128 on-chain. To avoid precision loss in JavaScript, they are serialized as decimal strings ( total_supply , valuation_cents , balance , total_amount ). - Convenience floats. Valuations also include a valuation_usd (float dollars) and percentages ( share_percent , claimed_percent ) for display. - Amounts are raw base units. Divide by 10 ** decimals to get a display value. The asset's decimals is included on each asset. - Cents. valuation_cents is USD cents; valuation_usd = valuation_cents / 100 .

title: API Overview › Endpoints
content: Plus GET / (self-describing index) and GET /health (liveness).

title: API Overview › Errors
content: Errors return an appropriate HTTP status and a JSON body: { "error": "not_found", "message": "no asset with id 999" } Status error When 404 not_found Unknown asset id 400 — Non-numeric :id path (rejected by the router)

title: API Overview › CORS
content: All origins, methods and headers are allowed, so the docs site and the web app can call the API directly from the browser.

title: API Overview › /stats response
content: { "total_assets": 1, "active_assets": 1, "tvl_cents": "500000000", "tvl_usd": 5000000.0, "total_holders": 1, "total_distributions": 0, "last_indexed_ledger": 3514152, "last_updated": "2026-07-09T08:43:12.101772791+00:00" } total_holders is the count of distinct approved addresses across all assets; last_indexed_ledger is the ledger the most recent successful refresh read from.

title: API Overview › Why REST instead of GraphQL?
content: The API only exposes a handful of fixed, shallow resources — assets, their holders, compliance summary and dividend history — so there is no deeply nested or client-varying query shape that GraphQL's flexible querying would pay for. REST also keeps the service dependency-free (no schema/resolver layer) and makes every response cacheable and curl-able with a plain URL, which matches the read-only, polling nature of the indexer. If a future version needs to let clients compose across many related resources in one round trip, GraphQL would be reconsidered then — for now it would add complexity without solving a real problem for this API's shape.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching
description: Rate-limit headers, ETag-based conditional requests, and Cache-Control guidance for the Stellar RWA API.
content: Rate Limits & Caching Rate limiting is keyed by client IP and uses a token bucket shared across API routes. Conditional requests are enabled on the /v1 data routes.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › Rate limits
content: Rate limiting is a token bucket keyed by client IP and shared across all API routes. The exact defaults are: Parameter Default Env var Sustained rate 5 requests per second per client IP RWA_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND Burst capacity 20 requests RWA_RATE_LIMIT_BURST Refill interval 1 token every 200 ms (1000 ms ÷ 5 per second) derived from RWA_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND The bucket starts full, so a client can send up to 20 requests back-to-back before any throttling occurs. After the burst is spent, requests are admitted at one per 200 ms — the 21st request in a burst, or any request that arrives before the next token has refilled, is rejected. This is a continuously refilling token bucket, not a fixed one-minute window: there is no per-minute quota and no counter that resets on a clock boundary. The limit is shared across API routes, so requests to /v1/assets and /v1/stats draw from the same bucket for a given IP.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › When the limit is exceeded
content: When a request arrives before a token is available, the API responds with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests using the shared JSON error body (see API · Errors for the canonical shape): { "error": "too_many_requests", "message": "Too Many Requests! Wait for s" } The number of seconds in the message is the time until the next token is available, rounded up to whole seconds (so it is at least 1 ). With the default refill interval of 200 ms, a client that has just exhausted its burst typically sees a 1-second wait. Retry-After is sent on 429 and is exposed to browser clients via Access-Control-Expose-Headers (see Browser clients ), but no X-RateLimit-* headers are sent. On 429 , pause for at least the indicated number of seconds when present, with a minimum one-second delay. Otherwise, use exponential backoff with jitter (and cap the delay), and retry only idempotent requests. For polling use cases, the indexer refreshes its state about every 10 seconds, so polling more frequently does not provide fresher data. Use a 10–15 second polling interval and back off promptly after a 429 .

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › HTTP caching with ETags
content: Snapshot-backed /v1 data endpoints return a strong ETag derived from the latest indexed ledger, along with Cache-Control: public, max-age=10 . /health and other non-data routes do not return these cache headers.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › How it works
content: 1. Make a normal request — the response includes an ETag header. 2. On the next request, send the value back in If-None-Match . 3. If the snapshot has not changed, the server returns 304 Not Modified with an empty body, saving bandwidth. The request still counts toward the rate limit. 4. If the snapshot has changed, the server returns 200 OK with the new body and a new ETag . First request — capture the ETag API_BASE_URL includes /v1, for example http://localhost:8080/v1 curl -i "$API_BASE_URL/assets/1" HTTP/1.1 200 OK ETag: "ledger-3514152" Cache-Control: public, max-age=10 Second request — send the ETag back curl -i -H 'If-None-Match: "ledger-3514152"' "$API_BASE_URL/assets/1" HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified (empty body)

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › TypeScript helper
content: const API = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL ?? "http://localhost:8080/v1"; const etagCache = new Map (); const url = ${API}${path} ; const cached = etagCache.get(url); const headers: HeadersInit = cached ? { "If-None-Match": cached.etag } : {}; const res = await fetch(url, { headers }); if (res.status === 304 && cached) { // Server confirmed nothing changed — reuse the cached body. return cached.data as T; } if (!res.ok) throw new Error( API ${res.status} ); const data = (await res.json()) as T; const etag = res.headers.get("ETag"); if (etag) etagCache.set(url, { etag, data }); return data; }

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › Browser clients: exposed CORS headers
content: The helper above works from a browser only because the API opts the relevant headers into CORS. ETag and Retry-After are not CORS-safelisted response headers, so without Access-Control-Expose-Headers a cross-origin res.headers.get("ETag") returns null and the cache is never populated. The API sets the following on every CORS response: Header Direction Why ETag exposed to JS Read after a fetch to store the tag for the next If-None-Match . Retry-After exposed to JS Read from a 429 to learn how long to wait before retrying. Cache-Control exposed to JS Lets a client decide whether to serve a response from its own cache. If-None-Match is likewise not safelisted as a request header, so setting it from a script triggers an OPTIONS preflight. The API answers that preflight with Access-Control-Allow-Headers: content-type, if-none-match ; both are required for the conditional-request flow above to work in a browser. // The preflight a browser sends before a request carrying If-None-Match. // Access-Control-Allow-Headers must list if-none-match or the request fails. OPTIONS /v1/assets/1 Origin: http://localhost:3000 Access-Control-Request-Method: GET Access-Control-Request-Headers: if-none-match If you self-host the API and call it from another origin, add that origin to RWA_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma-separated). Both the web app and these docs are separate origins from the API, so without it the browser blocks the response entirely.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › Which endpoints support ETags?
content: All snapshot-backed /v1 read endpoints support ETags. The /health endpoint does not return an ETag because liveness probes should always get a fresh response. Endpoint ETag GET /stats ✅ GET /events ✅ GET /assets ✅ GET /assets/:id ✅ GET /assets/:id/holders ✅ GET /assets/:id/compliance ✅ GET /assets/:id/dividends ✅ GET /assets/:id/distributions/:did ✅ GET /holders/:address ✅ GET /holders/:address/compliance ✅ GET /compliance/:address ✅ GET /health ❌

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › Cache-Control
content: The API sets Cache-Control: public, max-age=10 on snapshot-backed responses, matching the indexer's approximately 10-second refresh interval. If you are fronting the API with a CDN, configure it to forward the If-None-Match / ETag headers so conditional requests reach the origin rather than being absorbed by the CDN's own cache.

title: API · Rate Limits & Caching › Recommendations for integrators
content: - Poll at the refresh interval. The indexer rebuilds state every ~10 seconds. Polling more frequently wastes budget without gaining fresher data. A 10–15 s interval is a good default. - Use ETags for asset detail pages. Asset metadata rarely changes. Send If-None-Match on every poll — most responses will be 304 . - Handle 429 responses. Back off with jitter; the API does not expose a remaining-request counter. - Cache locally for read-heavy UIs. If your frontend renders the same data across multiple components, fetch once and share the result rather than making one request per component. - Prefer the API over direct Soroban RPC for display data. The API reduces the number of outbound RPC calls your integration makes and returns pre-decoded JSON. Use direct RPC only when you need live data that has not been indexed yet.

description: Correlate a response with server logs using the request id.
content: Request IDs & logging Every response carries an X-Request-Id header. Send your own X-Request-Id (up to 64 characters of letters, digits, - and _ ) to have it reused. The request id is carried only in the X-Request-Id response header (and in the server logs described below). It is not included in JSON error bodies — those contain exactly error and message : { "error": "not_found", "message": "Asset 7 not found" } See API · Error Bodies for the canonical error shape. The server logs one structured line per request inside a span carrying request_id , method and path , with status , latency_ms , indexed_ledger and consecutive_failures , so a report can be matched to the indexer state at that moment. Set RUST_LOG to control verbosity.

title: API · Contract ABI Versions
description: Supported contract ABI versions for each RWA contract type.
content: Contract ABI Versions The indexer checks each contract's version() return value at the start of every refresh cycle. If a contract reports a version outside the supported range the refresh is aborted and the last good snapshot continues to be served. Each contract type is checked independently against its own range, so a backwards-compatible bump in one contract does not affect the others and a rolling upgrade window can accept both the old and new version simultaneously.

title: API · Contract ABI Versions › Supported version ranges
content: Contract Supported versions Notes registry 1..=1 Stable; pinned to v1 compliance 1..=1 Stable; pinned to v1 asset-token 1..=1 Stable; pinned to v1 dividend 1..=3 v3 added snapshot-based claim/cancel The ranges listed here match stellar-rwa-contracts main as of this release. Refer to DEPLOYMENTS.md in the contracts repository for the deployed contract IDs and their exact version constants.

title: API · Contract ABI Versions › What happens on a version mismatch
description: What happens on a version mismatch
content: When the indexer encounters a version outside its supported range it logs a structured error at the WARN level and returns early from the refresh cycle: WARN rwa_api::indexer: ABI version check failed contract="CAR4XY3CEBQWFOL27JEWFW34KXSIZA7RFKDQMEIV7ZU723RWY37I2SYX" label="dividend" actual=4 supported_min=1 supported_max=3 The error message format is: {contract} ABI version {actual} is not in supported range {min}..={max} The /health endpoint will reflect degraded state once the number of consecutive failures reaches the stale-data threshold. The last successfully indexed snapshot continues to be served until a compatible version is deployed or the indexer is upgraded. When an ABI-version failure causes a request to fail, the response uses the shared error body shape (for example service_unavailable while the indexer is degraded, or internal_server_error for unexpected failures). See Errors for the canonical shape and the full list of codes. If you deploy a contract with a new VERSION constant that falls outside the indexer's supported range, the indexer will stop refreshing. You must either: 1. Upgrade the indexer to a version whose range includes the new contract version, or 2. Keep the deployed contract version within the range the running indexer supports. Coordinate contract upgrades with indexer upgrades in production environments.

title: API · Contract ABI Versions › Overriding ranges in tests
content: The AbiExpectation struct is public. Integration tests that need to test against a stub contract returning a specific version can construct a custom expectation and pass it to AppState : use stellar_rwa_api::indexer::{AbiExpectation, AppState, Config}; let abi = AbiExpectation { registry: 1..=1, dividend: 1..=99, // accept any future test version asset_token: 1..=1, compliance: 1..=1, }; // AppState::new_with_abi(config, metrics, abi) — see the indexer docs.

title: Architecture
description: How the indexer, API, and web app fit together, and what performance to expect.
content: Architecture The system has three parts — contracts, API, and web app — connected as described in Getting Started . This page focuses on the API's internals and the performance envelope integrators should plan around.

title: Architecture › The indexer
content: api/src/indexer/mod.rs runs a background task that polls Soroban RPC every POLL_INTERVAL (**10 seconds**) via simulateTransaction view calls, decodes the returned ScVal s, and swaps in a new immutable snapshot behind an ArcSwap . There is no database in v1 — every GET request clones the current snapshot out of memory. A single failed read is retried in place up to MAX_READ_ATTEMPTS (4 attempts) with jittered exponential backoff between RETRY_BASE_DELAY (150ms) and RETRY_MAX_DELAY (2s), so a transient RPC blip does not fail a whole refresh cycle. If a full cycle still fails, the API keeps serving the last good snapshot rather than erroring.

title: Architecture › Performance and SLO expectations
content: These are the concrete numbers integrators can design around today: Characteristic Value Source Indexer poll interval 10s ( POLL_INTERVAL ) api/src/indexer/mod.rs Max data staleness (healthy indexer) ~10s, bounded by poll interval api/src/indexer/mod.rs Snapshot read latency Sub-millisecond — an Arc clone of an in-memory structure, no I/O api/src/indexer/mod.rs ( snapshot() ) HTTP response time (cache hit, 304 ) Single comparison, no snapshot clone api/src/routes/mod.rs ( cache_headers ) HTTP response time (cache miss) Dominated by JSON serialization of the snapshot, not RPC — typically single-digit milliseconds for the Testnet dataset sizes api/src/routes/stats.rs , routes/assets.rs Per-IP rate limit 5 req/s sustained, burst of 20 api/src/routes/mod.rs ( RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND , RATE_LIMIT_BURST ) Cache freshness header Cache-Control: public, max-age=10 on all snapshot-backed endpoints api/src/routes/mod.rs ( insert_cache_headers ) RPC read retries before failing a refresh 4 attempts, 150ms–2s backoff api/src/indexer/mod.rs ( MAX_READ_ATTEMPTS , RETRY_BASE_DELAY , RETRY_MAX_DELAY ) These numbers describe the indexer and transport layer. The dominant cost at scale is rebuilding the snapshot once per poll cycle as the number of assets, holders, and distributions grows — see Performance / Benchmarks for how that scaling characteristic is (and should be) measured.

title: Architecture › What this means for integrators
content: - Don't poll the API faster than once per POLL_INTERVAL (10s) expecting new data — you will just get 304 Not Modified or an identical body. - Budget for the per-IP rate limit (5 req/s, burst 20) if you fan out requests across multiple assets; batch via a shared client where possible. - Treat last_updated on GET /stats (see API Overview → Data freshness ) as the authoritative staleness signal rather than assuming a fixed 10s bound — a degraded RPC backend can push it further out, and the API will still answer with 200 OK .

title: Compliance Guide
description: The core of an RWA platform — allowlists, transfer gating, jurisdictions, KYC expiry.
content: Compliance Guide Compliance is what separates a real-world asset platform from a plain token factory. Anyone can mint a token; the hard part — and the regulated part — is controlling who is allowed to hold it . This guide explains the compliance model end to end: why it exists, how the allowlist works, how the on-chain transfer gate is enforced, and how issuers should operate it.

title: Compliance Guide › Why compliance matters for RWA
content: A real-world asset — equity in a building, a trade invoice, a warehouse of copper — is almost always a regulated instrument . The law in most jurisdictions restricts who may own it: accredited investors only, residents of permitted countries only, parties who have cleared KYC/AML checks only. If those restrictions live only in a web app, they are worthless — anyone can call the contract directly and bypass the UI. For a token to credibly represent a regulated asset, the restriction must be enforced by the asset itself , at the protocol level, on every transfer. That is exactly what this platform does. An RWA token can only ever be held by an address the issuer has explicitly approved — and the token enforces that on-chain, on every single transfer, by asking a separate compliance contract for permission.

title: Compliance Guide › How the allowlist model works
content: The compliance contract maintains a KYC allowlist : a set of KycRecord s, one per address. Each record carries: - a status — Approved , Pending , Rejected , or Suspended - a jurisdiction — an ISO country code ( US , KE , DE , …) - a verified_at ledger and an expires_at ledger ( 0 = never expires) Only the compliance admin (the issuer or their compliance officer) can change the allowlist, via add_to_allowlist , suspend , and remove . Adding an address sets its status to Approved ; suspending flips it to Suspended but keeps the record for audit; removing deletes it entirely. An address is permitted to hold or receive the asset only if is_allowed returns true , which requires all three of: 1. status is Approved , 2. the approval has not expired, and 3. the address's jurisdiction is not blocked.

title: Compliance Guide › How transfer gating works
content: This is the mechanism that makes the whole thing enforceable. The asset-token contract does not trust any off-chain system; on every transfer it makes cross-contract calls into the compliance contract for both parties: transfer(from, to, amount) ├─ from.require_auth() ├─ assert !paused ├─ compliance.is_allowed(from) ── cross-contract call ──▶ compliance contract ├─ compliance.is_allowed(to) ── cross-contract call ──▶ compliance contract └─ move balances + emit event If either is_allowed returns false , the transaction reverts — no balance moves, no event is emitted, the transfer simply cannot happen. The same check gates mint on the recipient, so tokens can never be minted into a non-approved wallet in the first place. Because the asset token depends only on the compliance interface ( is_allowed ), the concrete compliance contract can be swapped with set_compliance — for example to migrate to a stricter policy — without redeploying the token. Try to transfer the sample asset to an address that isn't on the allowlist. The transaction fails with RecipientNotCompliant (8) . That failure is the product working — the gate is doing its job.

title: Compliance Guide › What a failed gate looks like
description: What a failed gate looks like
content: Contract error Meaning SenderNotCompliant (7) The from address failed is_allowed RecipientNotCompliant (8) The to address failed is_allowed Paused (6) Transfers are globally halted by the issuer

title: Compliance Guide › Jurisdiction restrictions
content: Beyond per-address control, issuers can block entire jurisdictions . Calling block_jurisdiction("US") makes every approved address whose record says US fail is_allowed immediately — without editing a single individual record. Unblocking with unblock_jurisdiction("US") restores them. This models a common real-world requirement: a regulatory change, sanction, or offering restriction that must apply to a whole country at once. Because the check happens inside is_allowed at read time, the effect is instantaneous and retroactive — there is no list to re-scan and no window where stale approvals still work. The API's /assets/:id/compliance endpoint surfaces the jurisdiction distribution (as counts) so issuers can audit their geographic exposure before making such a change.

title: Compliance Guide › KYC expiry and suspension
content: Approvals are not forever. Two mechanisms let issuers keep the allowlist current: - Expiry. add_to_allowlist takes an expires_at ledger. Once the current ledger reaches it, is_allowed returns false automatically — the holder can no longer transfer, and cannot receive more, until re-approved. An expires_at of 0 means the approval never expires. Because time is measured in ledger sequence numbers (~5 seconds each), a one-year approval is roughly +6,300,000 ledgers from now. - Suspension. suspend(address) sets the status to Suspended while keeping the record. This is the right tool for a temporary hold — a pending re-review, a compliance flag — because it is reversible with add_to_allowlist and preserves the audit trail. Use remove only when an address should be erased entirely. There is no background job expiring records. The check is evaluated live against the current ledger every time is_allowed runs. An approval that lapsed one second ago fails the very next transfer — no cron, no lag.

title: Compliance Guide › Best practices for issuers
content: 1. Secure the compliance admin key. It is the single most powerful key in the system — it decides who can hold your asset. Use multisig and hardware custody. 2. Prefer suspend over remove . Suspension is reversible and preserves the record for audits; removal is destructive. 3. Set sensible expiries. Time-bounded approvals force periodic re-KYC and keep your allowlist from silently drifting out of date. Choose an expiry that matches your re-verification cadence. 4. Approve the issuer first. The asset token mints the initial supply to the admin, so the admin must be approved on the compliance contract before initialize , or deployment fails with RecipientNotCompliant . 5. Coordinate distributions with balances. The dividend contract reads balances at claim time. If you need a clean snapshot, consider pausing the token around a distribution window. See the Dividend contract . 6. Use jurisdiction blocks deliberately. They are immediate and affect every holder in the region. Review the jurisdiction breakdown from the API first. 7. Treat registry listing as self-attestation. Anyone can register an asset; the binding control is the compliance contract, not the registry entry.

title: Compliance Guide › Putting it together
content: The compliance contract is small, but it is the reason this platform can represent regulated assets at all. Every other piece — the token, the registry, the dividend escrow, the API, the web app — is built around the single invariant it enforces: > Only KYC-approved, unexpired, non-blocked addresses can ever hold the asset, > and the asset enforces this itself on every transfer. Next, see how issuers operate this in practice in the Web App Guide , or how to read compliance state programmatically in the Integration Guide .

title: Asset Token Contract
description: Compliant RWA token — every transfer is gated by the compliance contract.
content: Asset Token Contract A compliant token representing a tokenized real-world asset. Every transfer is gated by an external compliance contract: both the sender and the recipient must pass is_allowed before any balance moves. Minting is gated on the recipient, so only KYC-approved addresses can ever hold the asset. Valuation is stored in USD cents ( i128 ). Amounts are integer token units in the token's own decimals base. Testnet: CBMCWLSQSWUTLUJFCNBHNBSXMUM3XU7NAQ5TSNERW4HA4ZZBYHLG4ECZ

title: Asset Token Contract › Data types
content: AssetMetadata is the single instance record describing the token: Field Type Notes name String Human-readable asset name symbol String Ticker, e.g. MLOFT asset_type String real_estate \ invoice \ commodity total_supply i128 Base units decimals u32 admin Address Issuer; the only account that can mint/pause compliance_contract Address The gate consulted on transfer/mint asset_description String valuation i128 USD cents paused bool

title: Asset Token Contract › Decimals and precision
content: All amounts on-chain — total_supply , balance , and every amount passed to transfer / mint / burn — are raw integer base units ( i128 ). The decimals field ( u32 ) defines how many base units make up one whole token. There is no floating point anywhere in the contract. RWA tokens frequently use non-standard decimals (e.g. 0 , 6 , or 7 rather than the typical 2 or 18 ), so never assume a fixed scale. Always read decimals from get_metadata (or the API) and convert explicitly: human_value = raw_amount / 10^decimals raw_amount = human_value * 10^decimals Example conversion — a token with decimals = 6 : Raw base units ( i128 ) decimals Human-readable 1000000 6 1.0 token 2500000 6 2.5 tokens 1 6 0.000001 token (smallest unit) With decimals = 0 the raw integer is the human value ( 42 → 42 tokens).

title: Asset Token Contract › Surfaced in API responses
content: The REST API returns the same raw integer amounts alongside the token's decimals , so clients can convert without guessing the scale. For example, GET /v1/assets/:id includes: { "id": "...", "symbol": "MLOFT", "decimals": 6, "total_supply": "2500000", "valuation": 1234500 } Here total_supply is 2500000 base units at decimals = 6 , i.e. 2.5 tokens . valuation is always USD cents (scale 2 ), independent of the token's decimals . Apply the conversion above using the returned decimals before displaying any amount.

title: Asset Token Contract › initialize
content: fn initialize( env: Env, admin: Address, name: String, symbol: String, asset_type: String, total_supply: i128, decimals: u32, compliance_contract: Address, asset_description: String, valuation: i128, ) Initializes the token and mints the full total_supply to admin . The admin must already be compliance-approved to hold the initial supply. - Auth: admin - Errors: AlreadyInitialized (1) , InvalidAmount (5) if total_supply < 0 or valuation < 0 , RecipientNotCompliant (8) if the admin is not approved.

title: Asset Token Contract › transfer
content: fn transfer(env: Env, from: Address, to: Address, amount: i128) Moves amount from from to to . Both parties must be compliance-approved and the token must not be paused. - Auth: from - Errors: InvalidAmount (5) if amount transfer performs two cross-contract calls into the compliance contract — is_allowed(from) and is_allowed(to) — before touching balances. This is the on-chain transfer gate. See How transfer gating works .

title: Asset Token Contract › mint
content: fn mint(env: Env, admin: Address, to: Address, amount: i128) Mints new tokens to a compliance-approved recipient, increasing total_supply . - Auth: admin (must equal the stored admin) - Errors: Unauthorized (3) , InvalidAmount (5) , Paused (6) , RecipientNotCompliant (8) , Overflow (9) .

title: Asset Token Contract › burn
content: fn burn(env: Env, from: Address, amount: i128) Burns amount of the caller's own tokens, decreasing total_supply . - Auth: from - Errors: InvalidAmount (5) , InsufficientBalance (4) .

title: Asset Token Contract › balance / total_supply
content: fn balance(env: Env, id: Address) -> i128 fn total_supply(env: Env) -> i128 View functions. balance returns 0 for an unknown address.

title: Asset Token Contract › pause / unpause
content: fn pause(env: Env, admin: Address) fn unpause(env: Env, admin: Address) Halts or resumes all transfers and mints. Auth: admin . Errors: Unauthorized (3) .

title: Asset Token Contract › update_valuation
content: fn update_valuation(env: Env, admin: Address, new_valuation: i128) Updates the recorded USD-cents valuation. Auth: admin . Errors: Unauthorized (3) , InvalidAmount (5) if negative.

title: Asset Token Contract › set_compliance
content: fn set_compliance(env: Env, admin: Address, compliance: Address) Points the token at a different compliance contract. Because the token knows only the compliance interface ( is_allowed ), the concrete contract can be swapped. Auth: admin .

title: Asset Token Contract › get_metadata
content: fn get_metadata(env: Env) -> AssetMetadata Returns the full metadata record.

title: Asset Token Contract › Code example
content: Transfer with the JS SDK, going through the compliance gate: const token = new Contract("CBMCWLSQ…4ECZ"); const op = token.call( "transfer", new Address(from).toScVal(), new Address(to).toScVal(), nativeToScVal(10000n, { type: "i128" }), // 100.00 @ 2 decimals ); // build → simulate → sign with Freighter → submit

title: Asset Token Contract › Events
content: Topic Data Emitted by ("mint", admin) total_supply initialize (initial mint) ("mint", to) amount mint ("transfer", from, to) amount transfer ("burn", from) amount burn ("pause",) / ("unpause",) admin pause / unpause ("valuation",) new_valuation update_valuation ("setcomp",) compliance set_compliance

title: Asset Token Contract › Security considerations
content: - Admin is fully trusted for minting, pausing, valuation and swapping the compliance contract. Use a secure key or multisig for the admin account. - Gate coupling: transfers depend on the compliance contract being live and correct. set_compliance is powerful — pointing at a permissive contract would disable the gate. Restrict admin access accordingly. - Integer amounts: all amounts are integers in the token's decimals base; there is no floating point. Reject amount <= 0 (the contract does). - Pause is a kill-switch: while paused, no value can move. This is intentional for incident response and regulatory holds.

title: Compliance Contract
description: KYC allowlist and jurisdiction rules — the on-chain transfer gate.
content: Compliance Contract Maintains the KYC allowlist and jurisdiction rules that gate who may hold or transfer a tokenized asset. The asset-token contract calls is_allowed on every transfer (for both sender and recipient) and on every mint (for the recipient). Time is expressed in ledger sequence numbers ( u32 ), not wall-clock dates. An expires_at of 0 means the approval never expires. Testnet: CBUERYDM7DXTZLLKDBRJKUBPFJ7M4OSUN4T7XKUARU345RLXNAIQD2IU

title: Compliance Contract › Data types
content: ComplianceStatus — Approved Pending Rejected Suspended . KycRecord : Field Type Notes address Address The KYC'd account status ComplianceStatus Only Approved passes the gate jurisdiction String ISO country code, e.g. US , KE , DE verified_at u32 Ledger at verification expires_at u32 Ledger of expiry; 0 = never

title: Compliance Contract › initialize
content: fn initialize(env: Env, admin: Address) Sets the admin. Callable once. Auth: admin . Errors: AlreadyInitialized (1) .

title: Compliance Contract › add_to_allowlist
content: fn add_to_allowlist( env: Env, admin: Address, address: Address, jurisdiction: String, expires_at: u32, ) Adds (or re-approves) an address, setting its status to Approved . If expires_at is non-zero it must be a future ledger. - Auth: admin - Errors: Unauthorized (5) , InvalidExpiry (4) if expires_at != 0 && expires_at <= now .

title: Compliance Contract › suspend
content: fn suspend(env: Env, admin: Address, address: Address) Sets an address's status to Suspended . The record is retained but is_allowed returns false until it is re-approved. Auth: admin . Errors: RecordNotFound (3) .

title: Compliance Contract › remove
content: fn remove(env: Env, admin: Address, address: Address) Deletes the record entirely and drops the address from the allowlist. Auth: admin . Errors: RecordNotFound (3) .

title: Compliance Contract › is_allowed
content: fn is_allowed(env: Env, address: Address) -> bool The core gate. Returns true only if the address is Approved , and not expired ( expires_at == 0 now Every check the RWA token performs funnels through is_allowed . Understanding its three conditions — status, expiry, jurisdiction — is understanding the whole compliance model. See the Compliance Guide .

title: Compliance Contract › get_record / get_allowlist
content: fn get_record(env: Env, address: Address) -> Option fn get_allowlist(env: Env) -> Vec get_record returns None for an unknown address. get_allowlist returns every address currently on the allowlist (any status except removed).

title: Compliance Contract › block_jurisdiction / unblock_jurisdiction / is_jurisdiction_blocked
content: fn block_jurisdiction(env: Env, admin: Address, jurisdiction: String) fn unblock_jurisdiction(env: Env, admin: Address, jurisdiction: String) fn is_jurisdiction_blocked(env: Env, jurisdiction: String) -> bool Blocking a jurisdiction makes every approved address in that jurisdiction fail is_allowed , without touching individual records. Auth: admin for the mutating calls.

title: Compliance Contract › Code example
content: Approve an investor in the US with a one-year expiry (~6.3M ledgers at 5s each): const compliance = new Contract("CBUERYDM…D2IU"); const op = compliance.call( "add_to_allowlist", new Address(admin).toScVal(), new Address(investor).toScVal(), nativeToScVal("US", { type: "string" }), nativeToScVal(currentLedger + 6_300_000, { type: "u32" }), );

title: Compliance Contract › Events
content: Topic Data Emitted by ("approved", address) (jurisdiction, expires_at) add_to_allowlist ("suspend", address) () suspend ("removed", address) () remove ("blockjur",) jurisdiction block_jurisdiction ("unblkjur",) jurisdiction unblock_jurisdiction

title: Compliance Contract › Security considerations
content: - Admin is the compliance authority. Whoever holds the admin key decides who can hold the asset. Protect it with multisig and clear operational controls. - Expiry is enforced at read time against the current ledger — an expired approval fails the gate immediately, with no cron job required. - Jurisdiction blocks are retroactive and immediate: blocking US instantly freezes every US holder's ability to transfer. Use deliberately. - remove vs suspend : suspend is reversible and keeps the audit record; remove erases it. Prefer suspend for temporary actions.

title: Compliance Contract › Related API endpoints
content: The REST API in /docs/api/compliance is a thin wrapper over this contract. Each endpoint maps to a contract function: API endpoint Contract function GET /compliance/:address get_record GET /compliance/allowlist get_allowlist POST /compliance/allowlist add_to_allowlist POST /compliance/suspend suspend DELETE /compliance/:address remove GET /compliance/:address/allowed is_allowed POST /compliance/jurisdictions/block block_jurisdiction POST /compliance/jurisdictions/unblock unblock_jurisdiction

title: Dividend Contract
description: Proportional yield/dividend distribution to asset-token holders.
content: Dividend Contract Distributes yield/dividends to asset-token holders in proportion to their holdings. An issuer funds a distribution with a payment token; each holder then claims total_amount * balance / total_supply , paid from the escrow this contract holds. Each holder can claim a given distribution once. Balances are read at claim time from the asset token. snapshot_ledger records the ledger at which the distribution was created, for reference. Testnet: CAR4XY3CEBQWFOL27JEWFW34KXSIZA7RFKDQMEIV7ZU723RWY37I2SYX

title: Dividend Contract › Data types
content: Distribution : Field Type Notes id u64 Assigned sequentially asset_token Address The asset being paid out on payment_token Address The token used to pay (e.g. USDC) total_amount i128 Pool size in payment-token base units distributed i128 Claimed so far snapshot_ledger u32 Ledger at creation created_at u32 Ledger at creation completed bool true once fully claimed

title: Dividend Contract › initialize
content: fn initialize(env: Env, admin: Address) Sets the admin. Callable once. Auth: admin . Errors: AlreadyInitialized (1) .

title: Dividend Contract › create_distribution
content: fn create_distribution( env: Env, admin: Address, asset_token: Address, payment_token: Address, total_amount: i128, ) -> u64 Creates and funds a distribution, pulling total_amount of payment_token from the admin into the contract's escrow. Returns the distribution id. - Auth: admin (must equal the stored admin; the transfer also requires the admin's authorization) - Errors: Unauthorized (3) , InvalidAmount (5) if total_amount The admin must hold at least total_amount of the payment token and the transfer must succeed, or create_distribution reverts. Funds are escrowed in the dividend contract until claimed.

title: Dividend Contract › claimable
content: fn claimable(env: Env, distribution_id: u64, holder: Address) -> i128 Returns the amount a holder can still claim: 0 if already claimed, if they hold nothing, or if the distribution is empty. Otherwise total_amount * balance / total_supply (floored by integer division).

title: Dividend Contract › claim
content: fn claim(env: Env, distribution_id: u64, holder: Address) Pays the holder's proportional share from escrow and marks it claimed. - Auth: holder - Errors: DistributionNotFound (4) , AlreadyClaimed (7) , NothingToClaim (6) .

title: Dividend Contract › get_distribution / get_distributions_for_asset / has_claimed
content: fn get_distribution(env: Env, distribution_id: u64) -> Distribution fn get_distributions_for_asset(env: Env, asset_token: Address) -> Vec fn has_claimed(env: Env, distribution_id: u64, holder: Address) -> bool View helpers. get_distributions_for_asset backs the API's /assets/:id/dividends endpoint.

title: Dividend Contract › Claim expiry and unclaimed dividends
content: Distributions have no on-chain deadline . A distribution stays open and claimable indefinitely: claim never reverts with an expiry error, and there is no admin sweep or clawback of unclaimed escrow. A holder can claim at any time as long as they still hold a balance of the asset token and have not already claimed that distribution. Because balances are read at claim time, a distribution that is never fully claimed simply remains open with completed: false and distributed < total_amount . The residual escrow (unclaimed shares plus any integer-division dust) stays locked in the contract — there is no withdrawal path. If your product needs a claim window, enforce it off-chain (e.g. stop advertising the distribution after a cutoff) rather than expecting the contract to expire it. The API surfaces the open/unclaimed state so clients can decide how to present it.

title: Dividend Contract › Reflected via /v1/assets/:id/dividends
content: The endpoint returns each distribution from get_distributions_for_asset . An unclaimed or partially claimed distribution appears with completed: false and distributed below total_amount ; there is no expired flag because the contract never expires a distribution. Example response for an asset whose distribution is past its advertised cutoff but still open on-chain: { "asset_id": "CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC", "dividends": [ { "id": 1, "asset_token": "CDLZFC3SYJYDZT7K67VZ75HPJVIEUVNIXF47ZG2FB2RMQQVU2HHGCYSC", "payment_token": "CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA", "total_amount": "100000000000", "distributed": "75000000000", "snapshot_ledger": 1234567, "created_at": 1234567, "completed": false } ] } Here distributed ( 75,000 ) is below total_amount ( 100,000 ) and completed is false , indicating 25,000 in payment-token base units remains unclaimed in escrow. Clients that enforce a claim window should treat such a record as "expired for display" while noting the funds are still claimable on-chain.

title: Dividend Contract › Code example
content: const dividend = new Contract("CAR4XY3C…2SYX"); // issuer funds a 10,000-unit distribution in the payment token const create = dividend.call( "create_distribution", new Address(admin).toScVal(), new Address(assetToken).toScVal(), new Address(paymentToken).toScVal(), nativeToScVal(10_000_0000000n, { type: "i128" }), // 10,000 @ 7 decimals ); // a holder later claims their share const claim = dividend.call( "claim", nativeToScVal(1n, { type: "u64" }), new Address(holder).toScVal(), );

title: Dividend Contract › Events
content: Topic Data Emitted by ("created", admin) (id, total_amount) create_distribution ("claim", holder) (distribution_id, amount) claim

title: Dividend Contract › Security considerations
content: - Balances are read at claim time , not at snapshot. A holder who acquires more tokens after a distribution is created — but before claiming — claims on the larger balance. Issuers should be aware of this when timing distributions, or pause the token around distribution windows. - Integer division floors each share, so a tiny residual may remain in escrow after everyone claims; completed flips once distributed >= total_amount . - Escrow custody: funds live in the dividend contract between creation and claim. The contract only pays out via claim ; there is no admin withdrawal path. - No claim deadline: unclaimed dividends never expire on-chain and cannot be reclaimed by the issuer. Plan distribution windows accordingly. - Payment-token decimals differ from the asset token. Amounts here are in the payment token's base units (7 for classic Stellar assets / SACs).

title: Registry Contract
description: Canonical on-chain index of every tokenized asset, plus total value locked.
content: Registry Contract A canonical, on-chain index of every tokenized asset on the platform. Each issuer registers their asset-token contract here; the registry assigns a monotonically increasing id and tracks issuer, type, valuation and active status. It also reports total value locked (TVL) across active assets. Testnet: CBX5SMLTXX6JP4HA5GQIO2V6QM7WCUGL2GZ6D4U773HMRI6RXISKPUR3

title: Registry Contract › Data types
content: AssetEntry : Field Type Notes id u64 Assigned sequentially from 1 token_contract Address The asset-token contract issuer Address Who registered it name String asset_type String real_estate \ invoice \ commodity valuation i128 USD cents created_at u32 Ledger at registration active bool Excluded from TVL when false

title: Registry Contract › initialize
content: fn initialize(env: Env, admin: Address) Sets the admin and resets the counter. Callable once. Auth: admin . Errors: AlreadyInitialized (1) .

title: Registry Contract › register_asset
content: fn register_asset( env: Env, issuer: Address, token_contract: Address, name: String, asset_type: String, valuation: i128, ) -> u64 Registers a new asset and returns its assigned id. - Auth: issuer - Errors: NotInitialized (2) , InvalidValuation (5) if valuation < 0 .

title: Registry Contract › get_asset
content: fn get_asset(env: Env, asset_id: u64) -> AssetEntry Fetches a single asset. Errors: AssetNotFound (4) .

title: Registry Contract › get_assets_by_issuer / get_assets_by_type / get_all_assets
content: fn get_assets_by_issuer(env: Env, issuer: Address) -> Vec fn get_assets_by_type(env: Env, asset_type: String) -> Vec fn get_all_assets(env: Env) -> Vec Query helpers returning filtered or complete lists. These back the API's /assets endpoint and the web app's explore page.

title: Registry Contract › deactivate_asset
content: fn deactivate_asset(env: Env, admin: Address, asset_id: u64) Marks an asset inactive; it is then excluded from TVL. Auth: admin . Errors: Unauthorized (3) , AssetNotFound (4) .

title: Registry Contract › total_value_locked / asset_count
content: fn total_value_locked(env: Env) -> i128 fn asset_count(env: Env) -> u64 total_value_locked sums valuation across active assets, in USD cents. asset_count returns the total registered (active or not).

title: Registry Contract › Code example
content: const registry = new Contract("CBX5SMLT…PUR3"); // register a freshly deployed asset token const op = registry.call( "register_asset", new Address(issuer).toScVal(), new Address(tokenContract).toScVal(), nativeToScVal("Manhattan Loft", { type: "string" }), nativeToScVal("real_estate", { type: "string" }), nativeToScVal(500_000_000n, { type: "i128" }), // $5,000,000 in cents );

title: Registry Contract › Events
content: Topic Data Emitted by ("register", issuer) id register_asset ("deactvate",) asset_id deactivate_asset

title: Registry Contract › Security considerations
content: - The registry is an index, not a source of truth for balances. Supply and balances live in the asset-token contract; the registry's valuation is the issuer-declared figure at registration (updatable on the token via update_valuation , not mirrored here automatically). - Anyone can register an asset (auth is the issuer, not the admin). Consumers should treat listing in the registry as self-attestation , and rely on the compliance contract for the actual holding restrictions. - Deactivation is admin-only and only affects TVL and listing, not the token.
